name: Perfect Derma peel

lead: The Perfect Derma Peel is a branded medium-depth chemical peel offered by clinics. It is promoted for smoother, brighter, more even skin and for acne scars and pigmentation.
It is usually described as a course of treatments, each followed by several days of visible peeling.

paras: A blend of acids, including TCA, causes controlled exfoliation, after which new skin forms. Other included agents are described as targeting pigment and adding antioxidants.
Medium-depth peels can cause prolonged redness, pigment changes, sun sensitivity and, rarely, scarring. They are performed by trained providers.

chain: Acid blend causes a controlled exfoliation
Skin sheds over several days and renews
angle.text: A provider applies the peel to the face, the skin darkens and flakes over several days, and users aim for improved tone, pigmentation and texture. A course of treatments is typically described rather than a single session.

lead: The Perfect Derma Peel is a branded medium-depth chemical peel performed by trained providers in clinics and med spas. Providers and retailers describe it as a blend of trichloroacetic acid (TCA), phenol, retinoic acid, salicylic acid, kojic acid, glutathione and vitamin C, and promote it for evening out skin tone, softening fine lines and improving acne scarring and pigmentation such as melasma.

In looks terms, the goal is brighter, smoother, more even skin from a series of peels, with a few days of visible peeling afterwards. Medium-depth peels in general cause a controlled injury to the skin that is followed by shedding and renewal.[1] The brand-specific claims come from manufacturers and providers; no independent clinical trial of this specific product was found.
infobox: TCA, phenol, retinoic acid, salicylic acid, kojic acid, glutathione, vitamin C (provider descriptions)

paras: Peels work by applying acids that injure the outer layers of skin in a controlled way so that it peels and regrows; TCA is a classic medium-depth agent.[1] Kojic acid is described by the manufacturer as targeting pigment, and glutathione as an antioxidant and brightener.
No studies found. Research on medium-depth TCA peels as a category exists, but none of the pages reviewed report a trial of this specific blend.

Encyclopedic sources note that the deeper a peel, the more complications can arise, including photosensitivity, prolonged redness, pigment changes, milia, skin thinning and scarring, and that medium-depth peels are performed by medical providers.[1] Discomfort such as warmth or burning during application is common with TCA.[1] Sun protection and provider aftercare instructions are standard parts of peel care.
Peels like this are discussed in looksmaxxing circles under skin-quality work, alongside tretinoin and microneedling, as a professional option for tone and scarring.
